name: Brindlemere
blurb: A river-ford market town on the eve of harvest: a stopped mill, a sick child across the water, and a chapel bell that has been silent for thirty years.
contentNotes: All-ages. No real people, places or events. Violence is off-screen and mild; nothing explicit.

realism.rationale: Story keeps tracking light (bands, a coin purse, a clock) so the town can be played as a conversation. Raise Money, Gear and Vehicles to see coins, loads and carts counted exactly.

currency.label: Brindlemere coin
currency.note: A labourer earns about 16 bits a day; a loaf is 1 bit, a night's bed 8, a riding horse about 8 crowns.

custom.note: Every month has 28 days and starts on Hearthday, so a date's weekday never changes. Dates are written YYYY-MM-DD with the month's number (Goldmoon is month 8).

start.display: Marketday, Goldmoon 25, Year 412 of the Charter, early morning
start.summary: You have just led your horse into Brindlemere on market morning. Stalls are going up, the ferry bell is ringing across the water, and four days remain before the Reaping Feast.

places.name: Wend Vale
places.description: A broad green valley where the River Wend slows and spreads. Orchards and mill-ponds crowd the near bank; woods and grazing climb the far one.

places.name: Brindlemere
places.description: A market town of grey stone and red tile, about eight hundred souls, built where the high road meets the ferry. Everything in it is a short walk from the square.

places.name: Market Square
places.description: A cobbled square with a stone well at its heart. On Marketday the stalls go up before dawn and the whole vale comes to trade.

places.name: The Crooked Kettle
places.description: A leaning, low-beamed inn with a copper kettle hung crooked over the door. Warm, noisy and always smelling of onions and woodsmoke; there are six beds upstairs and a stable yard behind.

places.name: Reeve's Hall
places.description: The town's broad-windowed meeting hall. The reeve keeps his ledgers here, petitioners queue in the passage, and the framed Charter hangs behind the long table.

places.name: Wren's Cottage
places.description: A narrow cottage hung with drying bundles of yarrow, mint and willow bark. A kettle is always warm, and the back garden is a tangle of useful weeds.

places.name: Chapel of the Quiet Bell
places.description: A small, plain chapel with a square tower and a bell that no one has heard in thirty years. Candles, polished pews and a vestry off the nave smelling of beeswax and old dust.

places.name: Dunmore's Forge
places.description: A smoky, open-fronted forge where hinges, nails, knives and ferry chain come off the anvil. A bench by the door has worn smooth under three generations of loiterers.

places.name: Ferry Landing
places.description: A gravel slip, a boathouse and a squat toll-hut at the foot of the town. A flat ferry hauled on a rope crosses the Wend to the far bank in about a quarter of an hour.

places.name: Wend Mill
places.description: A three-storey mill on the river bend, its wheel as tall as a cottage. When it turns, the whole lower town hears the low thrum of the stones.

places.name: Hollin Quarry
places.description: A grassed-over quarry above the old apple terraces, where the town's first millstones were cut. Rough-hewn blocks still lie in the nettles where the cutters left them.

places.name: Far Bank Waystation
places.description: A lonely stone house across the river where drovers and pilgrims wait for the ferry. A lamp burns in its window every night.

places.name: Under the Chapel
places.description: Damp stone steps lead down into a low, cold room that smells of old water and wet stone.

characters.name: The Traveler
characters.role: Travelling hand-for-hire with a horse and no plan
characters.summary: You came up the high road at dawn with a tired horse, a light purse and an open mind. Brindlemere is the first town in three days with a bed and a warm meal.

characters.name: Hollis Garrow
characters.summary: A careful man with ink on his cuffs who knows every debt in town and carries the worst of them himself. He is proud of the town's tidy accounts and dislikes being asked about them.

schedule.activity: walking the stalls and settling disputes
counting the week's ferry fares with Tamsin

regard.note: Wary of her quiet questions about records.

characters.name: Tamsin Reed
characters.summary: Broad-shouldered, sunburned and blunt. She has hauled the ferry rope since she was twelve and trusts weather more than people.

schedule.activity: running the ferry through the market rush

regard.note: Her sister's son; she is fiercely protective.

characters.name: Joss Tamber
characters.summary: Floury to the elbows even on his day off, gloomy when the wheel is still and ridiculously generous when it turns. The Tambers have milled here for four generations.

schedule.activity: milling, or tending the idle mill

regard.note: Thinks the reeve fusses over the mill's rent.

characters.name: Marta Dunmore
characters.summary: Quick-handed, dry-humoured and always smudged with soot. Her forge made the ferry chain, and she is not above reminding people of it.

schedule.activity: selling hinges, nails and knives at her stall

goals.label: Finish the new ferry chain before the autumn floods
steps: Forge and temper the last six links
Test the chain with Tamsin at the landing
Fit it to the ferry rope on a calm morning

characters.name: Sister Ilsabet Vane
characters.role: Keeper of the Chapel of the Quiet Bell
characters.summary: A small, upright woman with a calm voice and surprising stubbornness. She has polished the silent bell every dawn for twenty-two years and will not discuss why it stopped.

schedule.activity: dawn devotions and polishing the bell
tending the candles and receiving visitors

goals.label: Prepare the chapel for the Reaping Feast blessing
steps: Choose a child to carry the first sheaf
Keep the vestry swept and its door shut

characters.name: Wren Aldous
characters.summary: Warm, curious and always mid-sentence. She learned her trade from her grandmother and charges what people can pay, which is often a basket of eggs.

goals.label: Keep her fever remedies stocked
steps: Mix a fresh batch of poultice
Find someone to carry what is needed across the river

characters.name: Odo Kettleby
characters.summary: Round, jovial and always polishing the same mug. He knows everyone's business, shares most of it, and has a soft, easily bruised spot for Wren.

schedule.activity: keeping the inn on market day

goals.label: Make the Reaping Feast the best the Kettle has hosted
steps: Order the first barrel from the brewer
Work up the nerve to ask Wren to save him a dance

characters.name: Pip Marlow
characters.summary: Tamsin's nephew: lanky, quick and forever coiling rope. He hears more than he repeats and has good instincts about who is lying.

schedule.activity: hauling the ferry rope and tying off

goals.label: Earn a place on the ferry as a true hand
steps: Ask for a coil of rope of his own

characters.name: Bram Hesketh
characters.role: Keeper of the Far Bank Waystation
characters.summary: A weathered widower who keeps the lamp lit and the kettle hot. His daughter Nessa is eight and has been ill for three days.

schedule.activity: tending the waystation and his daughter

goals.label: Get Nessa well
steps: Keep the fever down with cool cloths
Send word to Wren for a poultice
Keep the lamp lit for the ferry

truth.label: What the bell was guarding
truth.cue: The two charters do not say the same thing.
truth.truth: The Charter framed in Reeve's Hall is a copy made from memory after the Great Flood, and it omits the clause that gives the ferry and the mill to the townsfolk in common. Brother Anselm hid the original in the chapel cistern during the flood and silenced the bell so that no one would linger in the vestry; he died before he could tell anyone. Reeve Hollis Garrow found the omission last winter while auditing old tolls. Believing the town had no claim, he has been leasing the ferry fares to a distant lord's steward to pay the town's debt, and he is ashamed of it.

rewards.text: The player learns the truth about the Charter.

climates.label: Temperate river vale
climates.note: The storm on Goldmoon 27 is scripted by a rule; ordinary storms are rare in late summer.

lore.title: Brindlemere
lore.text: Brindlemere is a market town of about eight hundred people where the high road meets the Wend ferry. It was chartered four hundred and twelve years ago and has never been large or poor. Its farmers sell grain and apples, its smiths make hinges and chain, and its ferry connects the town to the far drovers' road.

lore.title: The River Wend
lore.text: The Wend is slow and brown in summer and fast and brown in spring. It has flooded the lower town twice in living memory, most badly thirty years ago, when it took the old bridge and half the mill lane. The ferry crosses where the river is widest and calmest, a little above the mill.

lore.title: Market Square
lore.text: Market Square is paved with river cobbles and centered on a stone well that is older than the town's records. Marketday is the fourth day of the week; stalls go up before dawn and come down by evening. Disputes between stallholders are settled by the reeve, usually within the hour.

lore.title: The Crooked Kettle
lore.text: The Crooked Kettle is the only inn in Brindlemere, and it has been the town's living room for longer than anyone alive can say. The ale is honest, the stew is better than it has any right to be, and the innkeeper's gossip is free. Six beds upstairs cost eight bits a night; the stable yard costs four.

lore.title: Reeve's Hall
lore.text: Reeve's Hall is where the town does its business: tolls are counted, disputes heard, and the year's accounts read aloud at Founders' Day. On the wall behind the long table hangs the framed Charter, the document that makes Brindlemere a town rather than a village and which every child is taken to see once.

lore.title: The Charter
lore.text: The Charter of Brindlemere was granted four hundred and twelve years ago. It gave the settlement its market, freed it from the lord's tithes, and made the reeve answerable only to the townsfolk. Everyone knows the Charter hangs in Reeve's Hall; few have read it past the first paragraph.

lore.title: The Chapel of the Quiet Bell
lore.text: The chapel's square tower holds a bronze bell that has not rung in thirty years. The town calls it the Quiet Bell. Some say the Great Flood cracked it; others say the bell was never cracked at all. Sister Ilsabet keeps the chapel spotless and the bell polished, and she answers questions about it with a small, patient smile.

lore.title: The Great Flood
lore.text: Thirty years ago the Wend rose in a night and took the old bridge, the mill lane and a dozen cottages. No one in Brindlemere drowned, which the town credits to Brother Anselm, the chapel's keeper at the time, who went door to door in the dark and then, people say, ordered the bell silenced. He died the following spring.

lore.title: Dunmore's Forge
lore.text: Three generations of Dunmores have worked this forge. Marta is the current smith. She makes hinges, nails and knives for the market, and she forged the great chain that holds the ferry to its rope. A bench by the door is the unofficial parliament of the town.

lore.title: Wend Mill
lore.text: Wend Mill has ground the vale's grain for longer than anyone remembers. The Tambers have run it for four generations. Its runner stone cracked at the start of this week; until a new one is found and set, the town's bread comes from last month's flour.

lore.title: The Wend Ferry
lore.text: The ferry is a flat boat hauled along a rope. It runs from dawn to evening, carries twelve people or a loaded cart, and closes in a storm. Tamsin Reed has run it for twenty-six years, with her nephew Pip. A crossing is two bits for a person and six for a horse or cart.

lore.title: The Far Bank Waystation
lore.text: A lonely stone house on the far side of the Wend where drovers and pilgrims wait for the ferry. Bram Hesketh has kept it since his wife died, with his daughter Nessa. The lamp in the window is lit every night so the ferry knows someone is waiting.

lore.title: Hollin Quarry
lore.text: Above the old apple terraces lies a grassed-over quarry where the town's first millstones were cut. Nobody has quarried there for generations, but rough blocks and half-finished stones lie in the nettles where the cutters left them.

lore.title: Reeve Hollis Garrow
lore.text: Hollis Garrow has been reeve for eleven years. He is careful, fair in small matters and tidy in his accounts, and he takes the town's debts personally. People respect him; they seldom ask what he is thinking.

lore.title: Tamsin Reed
lore.text: Tamsin Reed is the ferrywoman. She is blunt, dependable and unimpressed by weather, wealth or titles. She says she can smell a storm an hour before it breaks and has been right so often that the town sets its clocks by her.

lore.title: Joss Tamber
lore.text: Joss Tamber is floury, gloomy and generous in equal parts. He gives credit he cannot afford and complains about it cheerfully. When the wheel is still he is hard to be around; when it turns, he sings.

lore.title: Marta Dunmore
lore.text: Marta Dunmore is the town's blacksmith. She is quick, dry-witted and has forgotten more about metal than most people learn. She keeps a handcart in the forge yard that she lends to anyone she trusts, and she is a better judge of trust than the reeve.

lore.title: Sister Ilsabet Vane
lore.text: Sister Ilsabet has kept the chapel for twenty-two years. She is small, calm and impossible to rush. Children bring her their questions and adults bring her their secrets; she has been asked about the bell more often than anyone else in town and has never given the same answer twice.

lore.title: Wren Aldous
lore.text: Wren Aldous learned herb-lore from her grandmother and has been healing Brindlemere's coughs, cuts and fevers ever since. She charges what people can pay. She talks quickly, listens carefully and knows which of her neighbours are quietly struggling.

lore.title: Odo Kettleby
lore.text: Odo Kettleby is the innkeeper of the Crooked Kettle. Round, cheerful and always at work, he is the town's best source of news and its worst keeper of secrets. People who want something told quickly tell it to Odo.

lore.title: The Reaping Feast
lore.text: The Reaping Feast falls on the first day of Reapmoon. The whole town gathers at the Crooked Kettle for the harvest supper, the first barrel of the new ale and a great many toasts. No one works that day, and old quarrels are traditionally put aside until the morning after.

lore.title: Pip Marlow
lore.text: Pip Marlow is Tamsin's nephew, fifteen years old, lanky and always coiling rope. He works the ferry every day it runs. Pip hears more than he repeats, and the town's children say he can tell when someone is lying by the way they hold their hands.

lore.title: Bram Hesketh
lore.text: Bram Hesketh keeps the Far Bank Waystation. A quiet widower with a weathered face and a patient manner, he lights the lamp every night so travellers know someone is waiting. His daughter Nessa, eight, is the reason he rarely leaves the house.

lore.title: The Brindlemere calendar
lore.text: The year has thirteen moons of twenty-eight days, and every moon starts on Hearthday. The weeks run Hearthday, Plowday, Wellday, Marketday, Tollday, Restday and Feastday. Goldmoon is the eighth moon, Reapmoon the ninth, and the last moon, Longnight, ends the year in a day-long festival.

args.text: It takes a rope, a lever and most of the afternoon, but the stone rides Dunmore's cart to the mill.
